hypotheses.reasoning: notification-svc v1.25.0 heap climbs steadily from about 22:31 (78% -> 84% -> 90% after full GC, GC overhead rising to 50%, old gen not reclaimed), which points to a leak in messageCache. Heap hits OOM at messageCache.put (#142, #168, #195) and the container is OOMKilled each time (#143, #169, #196). Each restart re-warms the cache (#145, #172, #199), so the heap refills within about 2-3 minutes and the cycle repeats. While the pod is down or restarting, api-gateway gets 'connection reset (no healthy upstream)' and returns 502s (#153, #166, #180, #193, #200, #210, #224). Those 502s are downstream symptoms and are not cited as root cause. Template-svc, redis, and notif-db show no errors, which rules out those as origins. The notif-db slow audit_log query (#73) and the DLQ schema warning (#30) are unrelated background noise.

The unbounded messageCache growth may have been introduced by the v1.25.0 release, since the cache warm-up runs on every start. The logs contain no deploy event or changelog to confirm this, so it is the alternative framing of the same fault and less certain than the resource exhaustion reading.

verdict.recommendedAction: Roll back notification-svc to the pre-1.25.0 build if the leak came in with that release, or hotfix messageCache to bound its size or add eviction/TTL. In the short term, raise the memory limit or scale out replicas so the upstream pool stays healthy while the fix ships. Then confirm heap stays flat across a restart cycle.
